title: The app garden got better signposts
summary:
The app garden grew quickly, and the paths through it—from discovery to documentation—got easier to follow.

The catalog gained fuller, markdown-formatted descriptions, shareable category filters, request-based sorting, and badges for new, active, and Bring Your Own Pollen apps. A fix restored the apps page after its app-list source returned a 404. Community additions ranged from storybooks and music tools to benchmarking, chat assistants, and image generators. Finding something useful among all those apps is now less of an archaeological exercise.

A standalone OpenAI-compatible endpoint accepts text and image messages, runs Polly’s tool calls, and returns a final answer; streaming is not supported. Later changes made code and documentation indexing more resilient to input limits, markdown quirks, and restarts. Polly also skips unrelated Discord messages before doing reply checks or API work.

SlidePainter joined the community apps with generated-image slides, shared style prompts, reference images, Markdown configuration import and export, and PDF export. It arrived alongside a broad crop of creative tools for presentations, storyboards, filmmaking, stickers, image editing, and more.

The lineup added `qwen-safety` for text moderation. Proxied upstream 429 responses now return as 502, leaving 429 for Enter’s own limits, and chat completion errors surface readable upstream messages. During a provider outage, Imagen 4, Grok Video, and Qwen Character were removed from the registries; Wan 2.6 was routed directly through Alibaba DashScope and marked paid-only.
